verdict: Avoid new sponge iron and ferro alloy exposure in Raigarh; lend only to integrated, cash-generating units with verified power and working-capital discipline.
title: Raigarh sponge iron & ferro alloys: a note to the credit manager
narrative:
## What this business physically is
**Sponge iron and ferro alloys are power- and coal-hungry conversion businesses: you buy iron ore and coal, burn them through a kiln or furnace, and sell a commodity priced off scrap and steel.** Cash is made on the spread between input cost and realisation, not on brand or customer loyalty. Shyam Metalics' March 2026 sponge iron realisation was Rs 25,656 per MT, up 1.98% YoY, while volume fell 2.33% to 81,083 MT [2][3]. **So when a proposal lands, check the realisation assumption against that Rs 25,656/MT benchmark; if the borrower projects materially above it, ask for the customer contracts behind it.**

## Where value and cash sit
**Value sits in integration — captive power, pellets, and ferro alloy mix — not in standalone kilns.** Shyam Metalics runs pellets, sponge iron, TMT, ferro alloys and power together [4]. Its Q3 FY26 revenue was Rs 4,421 crore, +17.7% YoY, but EBITDA margin was 12.2% and PAT was flat at +0.1% YoY [4]. **So when a proposal lands, check whether power is captive or purchased; if purchased, ask for the power tariff and its share of conversion cost.** Working capital is the other trap: Agrawal Sponge ran average working-capital utilisation at ~91% for the twelve months to Sep 2018 [7] — old data, but the pattern holds. IIP for NIC 24 (basic metals) grew only 2.4% YoY [D]. **So when a proposal lands, check whether the borrower is mid-project; if so, ask for the project cost, funding mix and completion date.**

## Who to pursue, who to avoid
**Pursue integrated units with captive power, pellet linkage and ferro alloy diversification, and existing borrowers with demonstrated cash accruals.** Avoid standalone sponge iron converters, borrowers with high group-entity exposure (Agrawal Sponge had INR 13.83 cr, 15.6% of net worth, in 2018 [7]), and any debt-funded greenfield expansion in this price cycle. **So when a proposal lands, check group exposure as a share of net worth; if above 10%, ask for the repayment source outside the group.**

## How to grow safely and what to watch
**Structure new limits as working-capital lines with monthly stock and debtor reporting, and term debt only against commissioned assets.** Take every month: stock statement, debtor ageing, power cost per unit, and realisation per MT.
